installedBase.title: Installed base: da Vinci vs Ion
installedBase.content:
The cumulative count of da Vinci surgical systems and Ion robotic bronchoscopy systems placed with hospitals and still in service. This is the installed capital base that drives recurring instrument, accessory and service revenue every quarter afterwards.

For Intuitive Surgical: da Vinci 5 is now the majority of new placements (315 of 546 systems in Q3 2026) and is driving a multi-year replace/upgrade cycle on top of net-new placements; Ion is smaller but growing its base faster (+21% YoY vs da Vinci's +12% YoY) as bronchoscopy adoption is still early.

What to watch:

  • Placements decelerating in a region (e.g. China) versus the base still compounding elsewhere
  • Ion base growth outpacing da Vinci on a small denominator -- watch the procedure-per-system ramp, not just unit count

procedureVolume.title: Procedure volume and growth, US vs OUS
procedureVolume.content:
Procedures (thousands) performed on da Vinci systems, split US vs outside-US (OUS), against the worldwide YoY growth rate management guides to every quarter. Procedure volume, not system placements, is what ultimately drives the recurring instrument & accessory revenue line.

For Intuitive Surgical: FY2026 guidance is 14%-15% worldwide da Vinci procedure growth, down from a wider prior range, reflecting US deceleration (ACA subsidy expiration, GLP-1-related softness in bariatric procedures) that OUS growth (new indications, Europe/Japan da Vinci 5 rollout, China and Korea adoption) is only partly offsetting.

What to watch:

  • US growth rate relative to OUS -- the gap has been widening through 2026
  • New-indication contributions (cardiac, general surgery via SP) showing up as a floor under WW growth

revenueByProduct.title: Revenue by product line
revenueByProduct.content:
Revenue split into instruments & accessories (recurring, per-procedure), systems (lumpy, capital sale of da Vinci/Ion hardware) and service (recurring, contracted maintenance). Instruments & accessories is the largest and highest-quality line because it scales with procedure volume rather than one-off placement timing.

For Intuitive Surgical: the new EUP 2.0 volume-based pricing program and China charge-code cuts are deliberately lowering instrument & accessory revenue per procedure by an estimated 3%-5% (mix-constant) through 2027, trading near-term per-procedure revenue for broader adoption in high-volume benign procedures -- so this line can grow slower than procedure volume for a while by design.

What to watch:

  • Instruments & accessories growth tracking below procedure growth (expected, per the pricing program) versus falling for other reasons
  • Systems revenue swings driven by da Vinci 5 mix and ASP, not just unit placements

revenueByGeography.title: Revenue by geography
revenueByGeography.content:
Revenue split between the US and outside-US (OUS) markets.

For Intuitive Surgical: OUS has been growing faster than the US through 2026 (new indications, da Vinci 5 rollout in Europe/Japan, China/Korea adoption) while US growth has decelerated on ACA subsidy expiration and GLP-1-related bariatric softness -- a mix shift worth tracking since OUS still carries a lower per-procedure revenue base than the US.

What to watch:

  • Whether OUS growth is broad-based or concentrated in one region (e.g. China placements have faced near-term headwinds even as procedure adoption continues)
  • US reacceleration once the subsidy/GLP-1 drag laps

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Intuitive Surgical, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
